sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The shape is not smooth: FY2023 was flat at 0.2% growth with operating margin collapsing 21.6pp to 15.7% [D284][D299][F47], then FY2024 revenue jumped 125.9% and FY2025 another 114.2% [D338][D393].
The FY2023 trough came from $2.17 billion of inventory provisions tied to excess Ampere supply against demand expectations, particularly China [P35][P38].
The recovery was Data Center: FY2024 revenue rose 217% on Hopper shipments for LLM training and inference [P23][P25], and FY2026 growth came from Blackwell compute and networking [P8][P10].
Data Center grew from 19.9% of revenue in FY2018 to 89.7% in FY2026 [D598][D620], contributing 60.2pp of the 65.5% revenue growth in FY2026 [D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Gaming, once 56.8% of revenue in FY2018, is now 7.4% [D637][D659], contributing only 3.6pp of FY2026 growth [D661].
Profit outran revenue: operating income grew 60.1% against 65.5% revenue growth in FY2026 [D449][D448], with incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D475].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% in FY2026 against 64.7% net income growth [D452][D450], helped by a 1.2% lower diluted share count [D470].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits well above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% [F30][D462], and cost of revenue took 3.9pp off operating margin as it grew 91.4% against 65.5% revenue growth [D477][D465][D448].
The Compute & Networking operating-income increase was partly offset by a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase-obligation charge in Q1 FY2026 [P7].
Operating expenses rose 40.7% [D468], driven by compensation and compute infrastructure [P9], with R&D up 43.2% [D466] and SG&A up 31.2% [D467].
Net margin held at 55.6% despite the operating-margin dip [F70], because other income reached $11.1 billion on unrealized gains including the Intel stake [X120][P3].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026 [F100][F60][D435], the low end of the 0.88x to 1.70x range across the window [D380][D120].
Free cash flow was $96.7 billion, a 44.8% margin [F110][D432], with capex of $6.04 billion at 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A [F105][D431][D437].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8% [D474][D473], leaving days inventory at 125 and days sales outstanding at 65 [D446][D445].
Stock-based compensation of $6.39 billion was only 6.2% of operating cash flow [X80][D438], so conversion is not flattered by non-cash add-backs.
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion, just 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion a year earlier [D441][D442][D386], because cash and investments dropped 75.5% to $10.6 billion [D439][D471].
Investing outflow of $52.2 billion [F120] rose on higher equity investment purchases and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [P1].
Even so, net cash as a share of revenue ranks in the 83rd percentile of six semis peers, whose median is -13.9% [D844][D845].
Capital return was $41.1 billion, 42.5% of free cash flow [D443][D444], split into $40.1 billion of buybacks and $974 million of dividends [X150][X160].
Customer concentration is the main risk: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14%, both mainly Compute & Networking [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026, subtracting 4.1pp from growth, and its share dropped to 9.1% from 19.2% [D545][D546][D544][D541].
The Graphics segment's 25% revenue decline in FY2023 [D754] was a one-period cyclical event, now 10.4% of revenue and growing 57.0% [D746][D747], so it is not a live flag.
Data quality: product revenue members sum to 190% of FY2026 consolidated revenue because some are totals of others, so they must not be added [R2].
Gross margin: a further move below the FY2026 level of 71.1% [F30] would confirm cost pressure from the H20 charge and product mix; watch the FY2027 10-K gross profit discussion.

Net cash as a share of revenue: holding above the FY2026 level of 1.0% [D442] would show the investing outflow is not structural; a further decline toward zero would reverse the balance-sheet strength.
China revenue: a return to growth from the FY2026 base of $19.7 billion [S24] would reverse the 4.1pp drag [D546]; another decline would confirm the geographic shift.
